standard_prerequisites.name: The n-truncation as a higher inductive type
standard_prerequisites.statement: trunc n A is generated by |a|_n for a : A together with, for each r : S^{n+1} -> trunc n A and r' : prd x P(r(x)), a point h(r) and a dependent path s_r(x).
standard_prerequisites.use: The reformulation at source lines 519-521 works directly with these extra constructors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of n-types with a point
standard_prerequisites.statement: An n-type together with a point u is contractible at u: there is a contraction prd x (t x = u).
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces u and v at source line 523, which are the second and third data of the induction principle.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dependent paths
standard_prerequisites.statement: dpath P p u v unfolds to trans P p u = v.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what turns the contraction v into the third datum at source line 525.

core_obligations: Observe that the given g : prd a:A P(|a|_n) already has the type of the first datum, so only the second and third data of the induction principle have to be constructed (source line 519).
Given r : S^{n+1} -> trunc n A and r' : prd x: S^{n+1} P(r(x)), use the constructors to get h(r) : trunc n A and s_r : prd x (r(x) = h(r)) (source lines 520-521).
Define t : S^{n+1} -> P(h(r)) by t(x) := trans (s_r(x)) (r'(x)) (source line 522).
Since P(h(r)) is n-truncated, obtain a point u : P(h(r)) and a contraction v : prd x (t(x) = u) (source line 523).
Set h'(r,r') := u, which gives the second datum, and note that v has exactly the type required of the third datum once dependent paths are unfolded (source lines 524-525).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the obligation to the second and third data of the induction principle.
Build the auxiliary map t into P(h(r)) by transporting along the constructor path s_r.
Use truncation of P(h(r)) to get a point and a contraction, which are the remaining two data.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.3.2 at source lines 514-517: for any family P over trunc n A whose fibers are n-types, and any g : prd a:A P(|a|_n), there is a section f with f(|a|_n) := g(a). The proof (source lines 518-526) is not a citation of the constructors: one has to build two of the three data by hand, first defining t(x) := trans (s_r(x))(r'(x)) so as to land in the single type P(h(r)) (source line 522), and then using the fact that P(h(r)) is n-truncated to obtain both a point u and a contraction v at u (source line 523). Only then do h'(r,r') := u and the contraction v, read through the unfolding of dependent paths, supply the second and third data (source lines 524-525).
